name: King of Sepharvaim
overview: The King of Sepharvaim was a male monarch known primarily for being defeated by the Assyrian empire. Specific tribal affiliations or additional personal details are not recorded in Scripture. His significance is tied to his role as a conquered king during Assyria's expansion.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Sepharvaim' directly identifies him as the ruler of Sepharvaim. This title is straightforward and does not carry a unique Hebrew or Greek meaning beyond denoting his kingship over that region, as referenced in 2 Kings 19:13.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for the King of Sepharvaim beyond what is noted in his unique attribute as a defeated king. There are no listed relationships or descendants mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Sepharvaim is significant in the biblical narrative as an example of the nations subdued by Assyria's military might. His defeat underscores the historical reality of Assyria's dominance during the period and serves as a backdrop to the broader story of God's dealings with Israel and surrounding nations. This defeat is recorded in 2 Kings 19:13, emphasizing the extent of Assyrian conquest.
